PLAN YOUR REQUIREMENT

A useful brief.
A clearer next step.

Dimensional checks, component verification, assembly inspection and documented acceptance reviews.

Decisions to make early

Inspection starts with an approved reference. Identify the drawing revision, features to measure, acceptance limits and the reporting format you need.

What to agree before work begins

Agree measurement scope, sampling requirements, report format and how any non-conforming observations will be recorded.

BEFORE YOU ENQUIRE

Questions,
answered.

What is needed before a component can be inspected?+

Provide the current drawing or specification and identify the dimensions or characteristics that require verification. Include reference datums, acceptance limits and the quantity of parts.

Can inspection results be documented?+

State the required report format and traceability information when enquiring. The scope, measurement method and documentation to be supplied are agreed before inspection.

A CLEAR START

What to share.

Drawings, inspection criteria, reference standards and documentation needs.

Technical scope, material suitability, tolerances, inspection criteria, pricing and timing are confirmed after reviewing your requirements.

A CONNECTED APPROACH

Think beyond
one process.

Your project may need design, fabrication, finishing and assembly together. Include the complete requirement so each step can be considered in context.
